# TinyPrune

> TinyPrune is an open-source, local-first macOS app for automatic file cleanup using lifecycle rules, not a generic Mac cleaner. Give downloads, screenshots, installers and developer folders an expiry date, preview matches, and move expired items to macOS Trash.

## Product facts

- macOS 14 or later; Intel and Apple silicon are release targets.
- Normal cleanup moves files to Trash, never permanent deletion.
- Keep takes precedence over other rules and protects folders containing kept items.
- Preview evaluates matching and scheduling without moving items to Trash.
- Rules can use filename or folder patterns, age, and project inactivity. Developer templates support dependency and build folders such as node_modules.
- Core cleanup requires no account or network access and reads filesystem metadata, not file contents. Optional update checks in configured, signed direct-download builds use HTTPS; Homebrew installs update through Homebrew. Early unsigned builds update manually.
- Interfaces include the native app, Finder menu and tinyprune CLI with JSON output and configuration validate, preview, apply and export commands.
- TinyPrune 0.1.0 is published as an unsigned, not notarized pre-release. Install with `brew install --cask navig-me/tap/tinyprune` or download the DMG from GitHub Releases. Landing-page window contents are illustrative examples, not release/version or reclaimed-space claims.
- Website analytics are separate from the app: the marketing website loads Google Analytics and PostHog.
